paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu was dissatisfied with the way Hideyori was developing. Upbringing mattered far more than innate qualities, and without a wise mentor to guide him, Hideyori was truly unfortunate. But Ieyasu had not despaired. He believed that the lively, openhearted Senhime would surely bring Hideyori happiness. If Senhime could bring light between Osaka and Edo, Ieyasu and Hideyori might understand each other’s hearts even while apart.

paragraphs.source_en: As a child, Hideyori often clung to Ieyasu and called him his “grandfather in Edo.” Ieyasu thought that if Senhime could foster a bond like that of grandfather and grandson between them, he would also be able to guide Hideyori properly. Moreover, the knowledge that he had kept his promise to Hideyoshi brought comfort to his conscience.

paragraphs.source_en: On the night before Senhime’s departure, Ieyasu went several times to the inner quarters to see Lady Oeyo and his wife, issued instructions to Okubo Nagayasu, and reprimanded Okubo Tadachika. His thoughts were filled with Senhime and Hideyori, and he seemed constantly to see them seated together like dolls displayed for the Star Festival.

paragraphs.source_en: Horio Yoshiharu, however, did not have the warriors carry spears and firearms. Instead, he made them shoulder hoes and axes and follow closely in small boats behind the great vessel bearing Senhime. To conceal their purpose, it was said that three hundred laborers had been sent to cut down the reeds obstructing the river and clear a passage. In truth, they were there to protect the great vessel, which also had weapons concealed aboard. Every one of these seeming laborers was a valiant warrior.

paragraphs.source_en: When Ieyasu came to Lady Okame’s quarters in the western garden, Gorotamaru was sitting there with perfect composure, listening as his mother spoke of hawks, beginning with the bird itself and proceeding to falconry. Though only a little over two years old, his eyes shone brightly and his expression was remarkably determined.

paragraphs.source_en: Seeing Ieyasu at the doorway, Gorotamaru immediately fixed his little eyes upon him and greeted his father. Though the child spoke only a few words, they reminded Ieyasu of Nobuyasu in childhood, and a strange fancy suddenly seized him: could a person be reborn after death? If so, perhaps Nobuyasu had been reborn as his son once more.

paragraphs.source_en: Hiraiwa Chikayoshi, who bore the title Kazue-no-kami, had once been Nobuyasu’s tutor. When Nobuyasu’s willfulness led him to commit seppuku, Chikayoshi beat his breast and bowed his head to the ground, blaming his own inadequate instruction; he even wished to take his own life and follow Nobuyasu in death.
